text:
Alex: Heads-up — I'm prototyping a lightweight 'gatekeeper' service to centralize canary ramp decisions and automatic fallbacks. Thinking about the router <-> gatekeeper interface.
Mira: Nice. What's the minimal contract? need low latency.
Alex: minimal: sync call with request metadata, model variant, current weight, and an action: allow|hold|fallback|throttle. Response should be <10ms 99th.
Sasha: Curious about failure modes — if gatekeeper is slow, router should default to a safe path. fallback to previous stable variant? :thinking:
Tom: +1. Router must have an async hedging option and local cached policy. Local TTL for policy = 30s.
Lea: Observability — gatekeeper must emit decision_id so we can trace rollouts end-to-end. Also expose why (metric snapshots) not just allow/deny.
Alex: Agreed. Plan: decision includes reason tags, primary signals (error_rate, latency_p50/p95, cost_delta) and probe fingerprint.
Jin: How are signals computed? central aggregator or local probes? We saw delays when relying purely on central metrics in previous rollouts.
Mira: hybrid: local quick-probes for safety (latency, correctness smoke), central aggregated metrics for trend detection. Central can trigger hold decisions; local can trigger immediate fallback.
Sasha: We need a clear boundary: gatekeeper makes policy decision; runtime owns execution and circuit breakers. Keep stateful backoff inside runtime to avoid chattiness.
Tom: Agree. Gatekeeper returns policy + advisory score. Runtime keeps a sliding window and enforces circuit breaker thresholds.
Alex: Example policy payload (prototype):
```
{
  "policy_id": "ramp-2026-03-20-a",
  "ramp_steps": [10,25,50,100],
  "hold_on": {"error_rate": ">0.03","duration_s":300},
  "local_probe_ttl_s": 30,
  "rollback_action": "switch-to-variant:v1-stable"
}
```
Lea: Love that. Can we also include a soft-fallback mode where we mirror traffic to fallback but still serve small % from canary for signal collection?
Alex: Yes — 'mirror_pct' field is in next patch.
Oncall-Bot: deploy at 4132109890: gatekeeper-service v0.1 -> infra-canary.
Mira: Operational concern — cost. If we automatically fallback to a larger model for correctness, cost can spike. Need cost guard rails in policy.
Sasha: Policy should include cost_budget_per_minute and an enforcement signal. If cost > budget, throttle canary aggressively.
Jin: Rollback heuristics: require both local probe failure AND central error spike before full rollback to avoid noise. Also require consecutive windows (2/3) to prevent flapping.
Tom: TTLs: policy refresh 30s, local cache 30s, emergency bypass by oncall or DeployBot with reason.
Lea: Integration tests — we need a canary-sim harness that fakes probe signals and ensures router respects allow/hold/fallback within latency SLO.
Alex: I'll draft RFC next week. Questions for design: 1) keep gatekeeper stateless (easier to scale) or let it maintain short-term aggregations? 2) policy DSL vs simple JSON.
Mira: Stateless with streaming metrics -> decisions riskier. Maybe keep short-lived state for rate limiting within gatekeeper but keep sliding windows in runtime.
Sasha: For DSL, start simple JSON plus named predicates. We can evolve into DSL if needed.
Alex: Cool. Action items: I'll open RFC draft, add policy payload doc, and a test harness ticket. Lea, can you add observability columns we need? Jin, can you prototype the local probe hook in runtime?
Lea: Yep. I'll add a dashboard template and trace links. :eyes:
Jin: On it.
DeployBot: Note: remember to add feature flag for rollouts so we can disable gatekeeper globally. :shipit:
Alex: Thanks all — PR coming.
